Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Class DiscoveryPacket

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.DiscoveryPacket
public final class DiscoveryPacket extends Object
The LAN auto-discovery announcement, as a small versioned binary record. A node periodically multicasts one of these so other nodes on the same subnet learn that it exists, what it is called, which fingerprint it presents, and which TCP port to dial. LanDiscovery does the socket I/O; this class is the pure codec, kept separate so it is trivially unit-testable without binding a socket.

Discovery is a hint, not a trust decision. These packets are sent in the clear and are trivially spoofable - any host on the LAN can announce any nickname and fingerprint. That is acceptable because nothing here is trusted: the packet only suggests a host:port to connect to, and the peer's real identity is then established cryptographically by the NoiseXXHandshake (which yields the fingerprint) and pinned by TOFU. Only public, non-secret data is carried: a fingerprint is derived from a public key, and the nickname and port are not secrets. No private key material ever goes on the wire.

Wire format (big-endian): 

   u8  version      (VERSION)
   u8  type         (0 = ANNOUNCE, 1 = GOODBYE)
   i64 epochMs      (sender clock; used for TTL bookkeeping display only)
   i32 port         (the sender's TCP listen port)
   u16 fpLen        + fpLen bytes UTF-8   (identity fingerprint)
   u16 nickLen      + nickLen bytes UTF-8 (display name)
Instances are immutable and safe to share across threads.

      epochMs - the sender's timestamp
